claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he still in school, college, sixth form, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's actually left school now. But he recently signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I have a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**How long ago did Alex leave education, and when did he register with the careers service?** (I'm trying to understand if it's been less than 20 weeks since he left education/training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It hasn't been very long at all - just a few weeks ago really. He left school and then registered with the careers service pretty much straight away. It's definitely been less than 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have enough details now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation against the UK Child Benefit rules:

- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- Alex is 17 years old
- He has left education/training
- He registered with a government-sponsored careers service shortly after leaving education
- It has been less than 20 weeks since he left education/training

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service.

Since Alex is 17, has registered with the local careers service, and it's been less than 20 weeks since he left education, you would be eligible for Child Benefit during this 20-week period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on your circumstances, you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex for up to 20 weeks from when he left education, because he registered with the government-sponsored careers service.

**Important things to note:**
- This eligibility covers a **20-week period** from when Alex left education
- After the 20 weeks, your eligibility will depend on whether Alex enters approved education, training, or employment
- If Alex starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or starts claiming certain benefits in his own right, your Child Benefit will stop

You should apply for Child Benefit as soon as possible to ensure you don't miss out on any payments during this qualifying period. If you haven't already, you'll need to make a claim with HMRC.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit claim?
